newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to launch tender for air radar network.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to launch tender for air radar network.

text.p: Argentina will call a tender for the construction of a national radar network for its airports, Defense Minister Jorge Dominguez said Thursday.
The government will put tender specifications on sale June 30 and will open bids October 3, the state-controlled Telam news agency quoted Dominguez as saying.
"The program foresees for the first phase, which is made up of the basic tender contract, an investment of $185.3 million," Dominguez said.
The contract will be signed March 6 next year and the winner will have a maximum 26 months to complete construction.
The aim of the project is to increase security and to optimize flight paths in Argentina's expanding air market.
The Argentine Airline Pilots Association complained last month that shaky air traffic control systems have caused six near collisions in the country's skies so far in 1997.
President Carlos Menem signed a decree to privatize 36 of the country's airports last week.
Dominguez said the development of a national radar network will also boost Argentina's air defenses.
